Photographed 04/09/2014.



This is the lower of the pair of locks at the eastern end of the narrow Aylesbury Arm and the second lock encountered when leaving the main Grand Union Canal at Marsworth. The pair form a staircase lock where the bottom gates of the top lock form the top gates of the lower lock. It is essential when going down this flight that the bottom lock is empty so that it can receive the water from the top lock, and equally essential that the top lock is full when going up the flight.

Photographed 02/09/2014.



This view is taken looking back into the upper lock, now empty as the narrowboat descends. One of the centre gate quoins dated 18?6, as described in the listing, is visible top left.

Photographed 02/09/2014.



This is the upper of the pair of locks at the eastern end of the narrow Aylesbury Arm and the first lock encountered when leaving the main Grand Union Canal at Marsworth. The pair form a staircase lock where the bottom gates of the top lock form the top gates of the lower lock. It is essential when going down this flight that the bottom lock is empty so that it can receive the water from the top lock, and equally essential that the top lock is full when going up the flight. There is a side paddle, visible over the ladder railings on the right, that can be lifted to drain this lock.
